speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me understand the severity and origin of these symptoms, how long have you been experiencing them?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with diplopia that changes with gaze direction, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Routine_Blood_Work (including CBC, electrolytes, Creatine_Kinase, and Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies). REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Routine Blood Work - CBC: Normal; Electrolytes: Normal; Creatine Kinase: Normal; Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies: Present (elevated). Repetitive Nerve Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
